# Running on the R36S / R36H (ArkOS · dArkOS · ROCKNIX)

The R36S and R36H are RK3326 (quad Cortex-A35, Mali-G31) handhelds with a 640×480 screen, a D-pad, A/B/X/Y, L1/L2/R1/R2, Start/Select and two analog sticks.

> **Honesty note:** the ARM64 build and launcher were built from the same project that is tested on desktop and in a browser, but **I had no R36S hardware to test on**. The controller mapping below is a best-effort mapping with a fallback; the frame-rate target (30 FPS) is a design target that has not been measured on a real device.

## What the handheld build changes
* Renderer: Godot *Compatibility* (OpenGL ES 3.0) – the right choice for the Mali-G31.
* Resolution: 640×480 (UI is laid out for 640×480 when `--handheld` is active).
* **Low graphics preset** is forced: plain materials instead of the toon shader, no shadows, no glow, short view distance (110 m) with mesh culling at ~60 m, 20 % particle density, 7-segment spheres.
* **30 FPS cap** (`Engine.max_fps = 30`).
* Music is pre-rendered (`res://audio/music/*.pcm`) so no synthesis happens at load time.
* Saves/settings go to `captco/save/` next to the game (set via `XDG_DATA_HOME` by the launcher).

## Install
1. Build or download `CaptCo-r36s-arm64.zip` (see README – `tools/build.sh r36s`, or the *Build Linux ARM64* GitHub workflow).
2. Unzip into the **ports** folder of the SD card:
   * ArkOS / dArkOS: `EASYROMS/ports/` (or `roms/ports`) – you should end up with `ports/CaptCo.sh` and `ports/captco/CaptCo.arm64`.
   * ROCKNIX / AmberELEC: `roms/ports/` (same layout; start from the *Ports* system).
3. Make sure `CaptCo.sh` is executable (the zip keeps the flag; on FAT/exFAT SD cards the launcher is started via the front-end, which does `bash`).
4. Refresh the game list and launch **CaptCo** from *Ports*.

## Controls (R36S/R36H)
| Button | Action |
|---|---|
| Left stick / D-pad | Move |
| Right stick | Camera (or L2 / R2 if you prefer the keyboard mapping below) |
| **A** | Jump (chain 3× for a triple jump) · talk · swim up · confirm |
| **B** | Crouch → long jump · ground pound (in air) · swim down |
| **X** | Throw Capt · release a captured creature |
| **Y** | Hat spin · creature ability |
| **R1** | Roll |
| **L1** | Dive |
| **Start** | Pause |
| **Select** | Skip text · recenter camera |

### How the mapping works
Godot reads the pad through SDL-style mappings. The launcher exports `SDL_GAMECONTROLLERCONFIG` from `captco/gamecontrollerdb.txt` (button indices for the stock "GO-Super Gamepad" / "GO-Advance Gamepad" device names).
If your firmware names the pad differently or buttons are swapped:

* **Option 1 – gptokeyb (recommended fallback).** If `gptokeyb` (part of PortMaster) exists, `CaptCo.sh` starts it with `capt.gptk`, which turns *any* pad into the keyboard bindings the game already understands (A→Space, B→C, X→E, Y→Q, L1→V, R1→Shift, Start→Esc, Select→Tab, sticks→WASD/arrows). Disable with `CAPT_USE_GPTOKEYB=0`.
* **Option 2 – fix the SDL line.** Run `jstest /dev/input/js0` on the device, note the button numbers, and edit `captco/gamecontrollerdb.txt`.
* **Option 3 – remap in-game.** *Settings → Controls* rebinds the keyboard actions (works together with gptokeyb).

## Performance tips
* Settings → *Graphics* is already **Low**. Turn off *Camera shake* for a tiny CPU win.
* Boss arenas and the hub airship are the heaviest scenes; the 30 FPS cap keeps frame pacing even if it dips.
* If audio crackles, set `CAPT_USE_GPTOKEYB=0` (gptokeyb runs a background process) and try again.

## Pocket Edition on the R36S
The Game Boy Advance ROM (`captco_pocket.gba`) runs on the built-in emulator: copy it to `roms/gba/` (ArkOS/dArkOS) – no extra steps. The `.gb`/`.gbc` ROMs go to `roms/gb/` and `roms/gbc/`. Battery saves are written by the emulator as `.srm`/`.sav` next to the ROM.
